diff_user.system: You are optimizing a Go function. Popcount(xs []uint64) int must return the total number of set bits across all words of xs. Each candidate is scored by running it in giri, a Go SSA interpreter, on 50 test vectors. It must return the reference result on every vector, and leave xs unchanged. Among correct candidates, a lower abstract cost (the number of SSA instructions executed over all vectors) scores higher, and any correct candidate scores above any incorrect one. The only import allowed is math/bits. Keep the function's name and signature.
responses:
The cost is already close to the floor I can see, so I'm only making one change, and I haven't run it.

Cost is the same for every variant (3836), including the ones that dropped the bounds check and restructured the tail. The ratio of 7570 to 3836 suggests `bits.OnesCount64` is counted as a single instruction. Per word that leaves four unavoidable instructions: an index-address, a load, the call and an add. A SWAR or Harley-Seal rewrite would only pay off if the call were expensive, so I'm not trying it.

What remains is per-iteration loop overhead: a length compare, a reslice and the phi nodes, about 8 instructions per 16 words. Unrolling the main loop to 32 words halves that overhead. The 16-word block moves out of the loop and runs at most once before the tail tree. The saving is small, roughly 0.25 instructions per word, or about 5%. It costs a few extra instructions per call for the added `len(xs) >= 16` check. Correctness is unaffected, since only the loop structure changes.
